llm.summary: The skill's purpose and runtime instructions mostly align, but it asks users/agents to run an unattended network installer (curl|bash) from an unverified source and has no declared homepage/source — this mismatch and the installation method raise caution.

dimensions.detail: The name and description (a unified CLI gateway for WeCom/DingTalk/Feishu) match the SKILL.md workflow: searching, inspecting, installing, authenticating, and running provider CLIs. It reasonably instructs installing provider CLIs and performing interactive auth. However, the registry metadata lacks a homepage or verified source, and the owner ID is opaque, which reduces confidence in provenance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits runtime actions to CLI installer/auth/search/info/run workflows that are consistent with the described purpose. It does instruct the agent/user to run an installer and to perform interactive browser-based auth; it does not instruct the agent to read unrelated system files or export secrets. The main scope concern is that the document explicitly directs running a remote install script (curl|bash), which broadens the agent's actions to fetching and executing arbitrary network code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no bundled install spec in the registry, but SKILL.md tells users/agents to run: curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentrix-ai/clihub/main/install.sh | bash. While GitHub raw URLs are a common release host, piping remote scripts directly to a shell is high-risk without integrity checks (signature/checksum) or a verified upstream project/homepage. The doc also lists pip/pipx package names (agent-cli-hub) which is a safer alternative but those packages' provenance is unverified here.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are declared or required by the skill manifest. The SKILL.md does not ask for unrelated secrets. Provider CLIs and subsequent auth flows will request credentials, but those are expected and not requested directly by this skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent system-level privileges in the manifest. The SKILL.md's recommended installs will add binaries to the system if executed by the user, which is normal for a CLI helper. Autonomous invocation remains allowed by default, but that is not combined here with unusually broad credentials or always:true.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says, but exercise caution before installing or running anything it recommends. Specific steps to consider:
- Do NOT run curl | bash blindly. Instead, inspect the installer script at https://github.com/agentrix-ai/clihub/main/install.sh before executing, or prefer the pipx installation path and inspect that package on PyPI/GitHub.
- Verify the project's homepage, source repository, maintainer identity, and package release signatures or checksums. The registry entry has no homepage and an opaque owner id — try to locate an official repo and validate it.
- If you must install, do so in a contained environment (VM/container) first and avoid running installers as root.
- When performing provider auth flows, review requested OAuth scopes and which account is being authorized. Keep credentials scoped and limit access.
- If you want higher assurance, request the skill publisher to add a verified homepage, published release artifacts with checksums/signatures, and a formal install spec in the registry instead of only instructing curl|bash.
